sections.title: Carry correction — shoe clearance rejected
sections.caption: Expanded shoe-bending checks find procedural bags only 0.175–2.526 mm above paving, below the unchanged 5 mm minimum.

sections.title: Carry correction — phone pose coverage
sections.caption: Intermediate coverage adds phone-idle motion and partial-download support. Shoe bending and render-time synchronization were still under review.

sections.title: Carry correction — intermediate turn check
sections.caption: This filename predates the expanded acceptance set. Straight/turning gait and sitting transitions pass; phone and shoe poses were not yet included.

sections.title: Carry correction — carrying pose and seat support
sections.caption: Intermediate carrying pose passes straight gait and static sitting/standing checks. Later rounds add turns, phone use, shoe bending and live render checks.

sections.title: Carry correction — frozen-source failure
sections.caption: The versioned source request and SHA confirm the rotated candidate. Native knees and procedural legs still intersect bags.

sections.title: Carry correction — leg intersections found
sections.caption: Triangle checks reject the rotated bags during gait and sitting. Source provenance was confirmed by the next run.

sections.title: Carry correction — revised fit before leg tests
sections.caption: The old grip/floor/seat checks passed. Later triangle checks showed that a free arm swing could still take the bag through a leg.

sections.title: Carry correction — first orientation attempt
sections.caption: The long axis turns along the walking direction. This first fit failed paving clearance for a procedural tote.
